META.text: Meta fell about 6.5% after quarterly free cash flow plunged 91% and management raised the low end of its 2026 capital-spending forecast, intensifying concern that its AI infrastructure buildout lacks the near-term monetization Microsoft and Amazon demonstrated.

TSM.text: TSM fell roughly mid-single digits, mostly with the global semiconductor selloff as concerns over hyperscaler spending returns, Chinese chip competition and leveraged AI positioning outweighed its strong recent earnings; no new TSM-specific operating setback was confirmed.

NVDA.text: Nvidia fell about 2.9% as the semiconductor sector was whipsawed by deleveraging, Chinese competition fears and scrutiny of whether hyperscalers’ enormous AI spending will generate adequate returns; Friday’s Amazon-led rebound recovered part of the decline.

AVGO.text: Broadcom gained about 1.9%, outperforming the volatile chip sector, as Microsoft and Amazon’s strong cloud growth reassured investors that hyperscaler AI infrastructure demand remains real; no distinct new Broadcom catalyst was confirmed.

PLTR.text: Palantir finished essentially flat, with no confirmed company-specific catalyst, as investors largely waited for its August 3 earnings while broader software weakness and its high valuation capped Monday’s pre-report rebound.

SPCX.text: SpaceX fell about 5.8% to a new low as investors remained focused on its August 4 results and the subsequent release of roughly 911.5 million insider shares, while merger rumors failed to offset dilution and supply-overhang concerns.

MU.text: Micron fell about 10.6% amid extreme memory-stock volatility as fears of higher rates, Chinese competition and an overheated memory cycle outweighed evidence of strong hyperscaler demand; Friday’s 5.9% drop reversed part of Thursday’s sharp rebound.
